parsed.doc_summary: Part 2 of the NJ DCA Landlord-Tenant guide. It covers the Security Deposit Law, LAD source-of-income protection, state rent-control posture, and anti-eviction notice rules for rent increases.

rules.title: NJ Security Deposit Cap
rules.requirement: A landlord may require at most 1.5 times monthly rent as a security deposit, plus the first month's rent at lease start (2.5 months total). Prepaid funds such as last month's rent count toward the deposit.
rules.quoted_span: may not require more than two and one-half times the monthly rent at the inception of the lease, this includes the security deposit and the first month’s rent.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent deposit (max 2.5 months incl. first month)
rules.conflict_note: The statute section is not cited in this passage; 46:8-21.2 is taken from the known law.

rules.title: NJ Security Deposit Handling, Interest and Return
rules.requirement: Deposits are held in trust in an interest-bearing NJ account, and the tenant gets the interest. The landlord must give written notice of the bank and account within 30 days. The landlord must return the deposit with interest, less itemized deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends. A tenant can sue for double the amount wrongly withheld.
rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant
rules.key_value: Return within 30 days; double damages for wrongful withholding
rules.penalty: Double the amount wrongfully withheld plus costs and attorney's fees; $500-$2,000 civil penalty for willful withholding from assisted tenants

rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or discriminate in rentals based on protected traits, including source of lawful income.
rules.quoted_span: nationality, or source of lawful income.
rules.key_value: Source of lawful income is a protected class

unverifiable_exemptions: rooms in an owner or resident-occupied single home

rules.penalty: Up to $10,000 for a first offense

rules.title: NJ Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings exemption from local rent control
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control ordinances for 30 years after construction is completed.
rules.quoted_span: newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.

unverifiable_exemptions: government-subsidized rents may also be exempt

rules.title: NJ bar on rent increases to cover condominium conversion costs
rules.requirement: After conversion to a condo, co-op or fee simple ownership, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion. Increases for new services or amenities are allowed.
rules.quoted_span: rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the conversion

requires_unknown_facts: building converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act notice for rent increases
rules.requirement: Before evicting for nonpayment of an increased rent, the owner must serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase. The tenant may stay by paying a lawful increase, which must not be unconscionable and must comply with local ordinances. Rent cannot be raised mid-lease.
rules.quoted_span: before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase.
rules.key_value: Notice to quit and notice of increase required; increase must not be unconscionable

no_rule_findings.finding: New Jersey has no state law that establishes, governs or caps rents. Rent control is left to municipal ordinances.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents.
